L0@P0: First-in-Dog (FiDo) Cure Cancer Initiative
L1@P0: Clinical trial opening for dogs with
L2@P0: mammary cancer in 2023
L3@P0: A new trial initiative by the School of
L4@P0: Animal & Veterinary Sciences and the
L5@P0: Dame Roma Mitchell Cancer Research
L6@P0: Laboratories
L7@P0: Mammary (breast) cancers arise spontaneously in
L8@P0: female dogs, and these are like human breast cancers
L9@P0: in many ways. Like breast cancers in women, many
L10@P0: canine mammary tumours are driven by the hormone
L11@P0: estrogen. Drugs that target the estrogen receptor (ER)
L12@P0: are prescribed for treatment of breast cancer in
L13@P0: women, but these drugs have toxic side-effects in
L14@P0: dogs. Hence, surgery remains standard-of-care for
L15@P0: canine mammary cancer. However, surgery can be
L16@P0: debilitating for a dog, is expensive, and does not
L17@P0: eliminate cancer cells that have spread to other
L18@P0: organs, which can ultimately result in death.
L19@P0: The proposed trial investigates an exciting new medical
L20@P0: therapy for dogs based on a ground-breaking study
L21@P0: from the University of Adelaide showing that drugs
L22@P0: activating the androgen receptor (AR) are an effective,
L23@P0: durable, and well tolerated treatment strategy for ERdriven breast cancer. In humans, AR activation drugs
L24@P0: also have positive effects on bone, muscle, and mental
L25@P0: clarity. Our aim is to develop a safe medical treatment
L26@P0: for mammary cancer in dogs that is affordable,
L27@P0: improves quality of life and is also effective in treating
L28@P0: metastatic cancers that have spread to other organs.
L29@P0: Importantly, this study will not only benefit dogs with
L30@P0: mammary cancer but will also inform how best to use
L31@P0: this treatment for women with breast cancer.
L32@P0: The University of Adelaide Team
L33@P0: The team comprises researchers and animal care
L34@P0: staff with expertise in oncology, surgery,
L35@P0: translational research, pathology and clinical trials.
L36@P0: It is co-led by Prof Wayne Tilley, a pioneer of sex
L37@P0: hormone receptor action in breast and prostate
L38@P0: cancers and Director of the Dame Roma Mitchell
L39@P0: Cancer Research Laboratories (DRMCRL), and
L40@P0: Assoc. Prof Anne Peaston, a veterinary oncologist
L41@P0: and clinical lead at the Roseworthy Veterinary Hospital
L42@P0: (formerly the Companion Animal Health Centre),
L43@P0: Roseworthy.
L44@P0: What is involved for your dog?
L45@P0: There are 3 phases of the FiDo study. Discuss with
L46@P0: your vet the possibility of participating as follows:
L47@P0: Phase 1: Simple donation of fresh mammary tissue
L48@P0: removed during surgery will help to analyse ER and AR
L49@P0: action, including testing medical therapies using a
L50@P0: unique method developed by the research team.
L51@P0: Phase 2: Window of Opportunity Study – 2 weeks
L52@P0: before surgery:
L53@P0: A short study to determine whether there is a response
L54@P0: to an AR activation drug. Your dog will be randomly
L55@P0: assigned to one of 3 treatment arms: AR activation
L56@P0: treatment (T + Ai) through an implant under the skin;
L57@P0: ER target treatment used in women (Anastrozole; Ai)
L58@P0: with a daily oral tablet; or a placebo treatment. A
L59@P0: tumour biopsy will be collected at the start and end of
L60@P0: the 2 weeks to assess treatment response. Surgical
L61@P0: biopsy costs are subsidised, as are any additional
L62@P0: procedures outside standard-of-care.
L63@P0: Phase 3: Option to continue – up to 12 months:
L64@P0: A longer term study following surgery to examine the
L65@P0: treatment effects on quality-of-life, delay of tumour
L66@P0: recurrence and prevention of cancer metastasis. Your
L67@P0: dog will be randomly assigned to 1 of 2 treatment
L68@P0: arms: AR activation treatment (T + Ai) or standard-ofcare treatment. Over the next year, your dog will have
L69@P0: monthly check-ups, up to three CT scans under
L70@P0: anaesthesia, and re-insertion of a new AR activation
L71@P0: implant every 3 months under anaesthesia. If drug
L72@P0: resistance or cancer progression occurs after surgery,
L73@P0: your dog will go off the study and other therapy can be
L74@P0: considered with your veterinarian’s input.
L75@P0: For more information, email:
L76@P0: wayne.tilley@adelaide.edu.au; or
L77@P0: anne.peaston@adelaide.edu.au
L78@P0: Please add in Subject line: dog mammary cancer
